jobs.occupation: Doctoral Researcher / PhD Candidate (f/m/x) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description:
We are looking to support our rapidly growing team as soon as possible: Doctoral Researcher / PhD Candidate in Immunotherapy of Viral Infections (f/m/x)

Institute of Virology - Laboratory of Experimental lmmunology
TV-L: 25 h/week (64,94%)
Fixed-term employment for 3 years under the German Academic Fixed-Term Contract Act (WissZeitVG) for the purpose of pursuing a doctoral degree (PhD)
Your salary will be based on TV-L

Your tasks

• Contribute to research projects investigating broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs) to effectively target HIV-1 in vivo
• Design and evaluate AAV-based gene vector strategies for in vivo delivery of bNAb combination therapy
• Establish multispecific antibody-derived protein constructs to target the HIV-1 envelope protein
• Investigate bNAb expression, antibody-mediated virus neutralization in vitro and in vivo, and pathways of viral immune escape
• Plan, perform, and analyze experiments under scientific supervision using state-of-the-art approaches in immunology, virology, and molecular biology
• Establish, optimize, and apply immunological and virological assays, including cell culture, flow cytometry, ELISA, neutralization assays, molecular cloning, and next-generation sequencing
• Perform experiments using infectious viral material in vitro and in vivo (humanized mice) in biosafety level S3 environments
• Collaborate with national and international research partners in an interdisciplinary research environment
• Present research findings at scientific meetings and conferences, and prepare scientific manuscripts
• Maintain detailed experimental records and ensure high standards of scientific quality, reproducibility, and documentation

Your profile

• Excellent university degree (M.Sc. or equivalent) in biology, biomedicine, immunology, virology, molecular medicine, or a related life science discipline
• Strong interest in translational research at the interface of immunology, virology, and infectious diseases
• Hands-on experience with immunological and molecular biology methods (e.g., cell culture, flow cytometry, ELISA, PCR, cloning, or sequencing technologies) as well as experience working with small animal models are advantageous
• Willingness to conduct experiments using HIV-1-infected humanized mouse models (existing FELASA certification is beneficial)
• Prior experience in virology, antibody research, B cell biology, or HIV research is beneficial but not required
• Independent, structured, and detail-oriented approach to scientific work based on high personal scientific standards
• High level of motivation to independently address complex scientific questions and develop creative as well as innovative solutions for scientific problems
• Strong teamwork and communication skills, as well as enthusiasm for working in an interdisciplinary and international research environment
• Excellent written and spoken English

Our offer

• Participation in a highly modern and internationally connected research project with strong scientific and societal relevance
• An excellent scientific environment within a dynamic and interdisciplinary team
• Access to state-of-the-art technologies and laboratory infrastructure within the new “Translational Research for Infectious Diseases and Oncology (TRIO)” research center
• Close scientific supervision and support for your professional and personal development
• Opportunities to participate in national and international conferences and to publish scientific findings
• Challenging and diverse responsibilities with a high degree of independence and creative freedom
• For further information, please visit www.klein-lab.de
 
Your future with us

We are one of the leading university hospitals in Germany and network research, teaching and health care at the highest level. That's why many things are a lot bigger for us: the spectrum of exciting development opportunities. The limitless openness with which specialists from all over the world work together here. Or our commitment as an employer to support all employees as best we can in reconciling their job with their goals and life situations.
This is the University Hospital of Cologne: Everything but ordinary.

Your future in detail

We are a dedicated translational research group focused on understanding the fundamentals of human immune responses to viral pathogens and on developing novel strategies for the prevention and treatment of infectious diseases. Our work combines cutting-edge immunology, virology, antibody engineering, and translational research approaches to address clinically relevant questions in viral infections.
This PhD project focuses on the investigation of AAV-based strategies to effectively target HIV-1 using broadly neutralizing antibodies. A central goal of the project is to develop novel approaches for enabling in vivo expression of bNAb combinations that overcome limitations of AAV packaging capacity. The project will involve the design and detailed characterization of multispecific bNAb-derived constructs, the in vivo validation of AAV-mediated protein expression, and the analysis of antiviral activity as well as viral evolution in HIV-1-infected humanized mouse models. The successful candidate will work in a highly collaborative environment with access to state-of-the-art laboratory infrastructure and clinical research networks.
Your work will contribute to a deeper understanding of antibody activity against HIV-1 as well as viral escape mechanisms, and support the development of innovative preventive and therapeutic strategies.
Applications from female candidates are expressly welcome and will be given priority in the event of equal suitability, competence and professional performance. People with disabilities are welcome to apply and will be treated preferentially in the event of equal suitability and qualification.

We are currently looking for experienced nannies, babysitters, and tutors to work with families in Cologne and the surrounding areas. If you speak English, French, Italian, or another widely spoken language, we’d love to hear from you!

Your Responsibilities

- Provide loving, attentive, and safe care for children.
- Organize and structure daily routines with age-appropriate activities such as games, creative play, reading, or homework support.
- Accompany children to and from school, nursery, or extracurricular activities.
- Handle light, child-related housekeeping: meal prep, tidying play areas, laundry, etc.

Your Profile

- Experience with children or babies is essential. A background in education or childcare is a strong advantage.
- You’re caring, empathetic, and genuinely enjoy working with children.
- You’re reliable, organized, and flexible in your schedule.
- You have a friendly, open, and professional attitude.
- You speak English, French, Italian, or another common European language fluently.

Why Join Us?

- Bring your cultural diversity and language skills into a role where they truly make a difference.
- Get matched with families that value your skills and background.
- Be part of a trusted network of international childcare professionals.

If you're passionate about childcare and want to make a difference in a family’s life, we’d love to hear from you!

Apply now by submitting your CV directly on our website.

We look forward to welcoming you to the Native Nanny community!

jobs.occupation: Software Automation Engineer (m/w/d) – Semiconductor (AMHS) (Ingenieur/in - Automatisierungstechnik)
jobs.description:
About us European Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (ESMC) GmbH is
the joint venture between TSMC, Bosch, Infineon and NXP. For the first
time, global technology leader TSMC is building a semiconductor fab in
the heart of Europe, offering cutting-edge manufacturing technologies
for next-generation semiconductor products. ESMC represents a shared
commitment to strengthening the European semiconductor ecosystem. For
our future fab in Dresden, we are looking for a highly motivated and
committed: AMHS Software Automation Engineer (m/w/d) Optimize the
heartbeat of our production. As an AMHS Software Engineer, you are the
mastermind behind the control system of our Automated Material
Handling System (AMHS). You ensure that millions of transport
movements mesh seamlessly, eliminate bottlenecks, and take the
efficiency of our production line to the next level. Tasks Your
Mission: Maximizing Performance Through Intelligent Control: System
tuning & KPI boost: You analyze transfer data and optimize system
performance to achieve capacity targets and minimize process
variability. Seamless integration: You ensure seamless communication
between the AMHS, production equipment, and higher-level control
systems. Innovation & Automation: You design KPI monitoring systems
and develop solutions to reduce manual intervention (manual loading)
to a minimum. Project Management & Cross-FAB Leadership: You lead
cross-site projects to reduce costs and increase productivity—from
planning through to go-live. Team Mentoring: You will lead and develop
a team of technicians and engineers, foster team spirit, and share
your knowledge. Lifecycle Management: You will validate new software
features, lead annual upgrades and retrofit projects, and assist in
the setup of new fab installations. Profile You are a proactive
teamplayer who combines in-depth technical knowledge with leadership
skills and a hands-on approach. Education: Master’s degree in
Industrial Engineering, Computer Science (IT), Systems Engineering,
Automation Engineering, or a related field. Expertise: In-depth
knowledge of optimization algorithms, Industrial Engineering (IE), and
information technology (C#, Java, Python, SQL, Oracle, MS-SQL, VBA)
Experience: Professional experience in the semiconductor industry is
required Methodology: You are proficient in applying problem-solving
methods such as FMEA, SPC, and 8D. Personality: A goal-oriented team
player with leadership potential who keeps a cool head even in a
dynamic, fast-paced environment. Language: Fluent in English (company
language). Basic communication skills in Mandarin or German is a plus.
Training: Available for on-the-job training in Taiwan, 9 to 12 months.
Location: Dresden, Germany. We offer Each journey starts with a first
step. Joining ESMC at this early stage will provide you with the
unique opportunity to actively shape the future of the fab in Dresden,
boost your career and put your true potential to the test. You will be
working in a fast paced, international startup environment whilst at
the same time having access to the experience, talent, and resources
of the largest and most advanced semiconductor manufacturer in the
world, TSMC. You have ample opportunities to learn about TSMC
Operations, Digital Transformation, and various advanced Facilities
related topics, both in Taiwan and other sites around the world.
Behind the world’s most advanced technology are real people with
real passion. Our success is fueled by our core values: Integrity,
Commitment, Innovation and Customer Trust (ICIC). At ESMC we believe
in the power of inclusive leadership and passion. We demonstrate this
in our commitment to our people vision: create an inclusive
environment to inspire passion and enable the best in YOU. It is the
policy of ESMC to provide equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all
persons regardless of age, color, ethnic and national origin,
citizenship status, physical or mental disability, race, religion,
creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or
expression, genetic information, marital status, status with regard to
public assistance, veteran status, or any other characteristic
protected by federal, state or local law. Additional contact details
Please apply with your English resume. The ESMC recruiting team will
get in touch with you if your candidacy fits the hiring criteria.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher Position— Plant Membrane Biochemistry and Chemoproteomics (m/f/d)  (10/2026) (UX-Researcher/in)
jobs.description:
Your area of responsibility The question How does proteolytic regulation control plant plasma-membrane receptor function and plant immune responses? The plant plasma membrane is a dynamic hub for nutrient uptake, pathogen detection and stress signalling, anchored by surface receptors. In animals, proteolytic cleavage of membrane proteins is a major regulatory mechanism in immunity. In plants, its role remains largely unexplored. FRONTERA, funded by the European Research Council through an ERC Starting Grant, sets out to close that gap. The project combines chemoproteomics, cell biology, protease biochemistry and genetics, and looks at both sides of the process: the proteases that cut, and the substrates they act on. It is curiosity-driven research with a long view towards crop resilience and sustainable agriculture. Your tasks: You will lead the membrane biochemistry and chemoproteomics side of FRONTERA: establishing the preparations and the activity-based profiling needed to study proteases where they work, at the plant plasma membrane.
• Develop and optimise membrane preparation methods suited to downstream chemoproteomics
• Apply activity-based protein profiling and mass spectrometry to characterise membrane-associated protease activities, working with our in-house facility
• Relate biochemical findings to immune responses in planta, in collaboration across the group
• Co-supervise a doctoral researcher
• Present and publish your scientific data

Your profile Essential
• A doctoral degree in biochemistry, plant science, molecular biology, chemical biology or a closely related field. If your thesis is submitted but not yet defended by the start date, please apply and tell us your timeline.
• Solid hands-on experience in protein biochemistry
• Real interest in method development, including tolerance for the weeks when a protocol refuses to work
• Interest in mentoring a doctoral researcher
• Excellent English language skills, written and spoken. German is not required.

Desirable
• Membrane protein handling, subcellular fractionation or membrane isolation
• Activity-based protein profiling, chemical probes or related chemical biology
• LC-MS/MS proteomics, from sample preparation to data analysis
• Work with plant systems, including transient expression
• Proteomics data analysis (MaxQuant, FragPipe, Perseus, R, Python)
• Supervision or teaching experience

Read the second list as a description of the project, not a test. Nobody arrives with all of it. Candidates who would do this job well routinely talk themselves out of applying because they match four points instead of six. If the science interests you and you bring the essentials, we would like to see your application. Tell us in your cover letter what you would need to learn.

We offer
• Modern Working Conditions: Comprehensive introduction to work techniques and a modern research environment with state-of-the-art equipment and up-to-date software
• Career Development: Targeted training opportunities and access to a specialized library with electronic resources and quiet workspaces
• Compensation & Security: Classification according to TV-L including annual bonus, pension scheme (VBL), health offers, and discounted canteen meals
• Ideal Working Environment: A varied and inspiring workplace in an international setting at a leading scientific and innovation hub
• Team Spirit and Leadership Culture: An open culture that strengthens teamwork, enables career networking, and promotes your research skills.
• Work-Life Balance: Flexible working models, remote work options, and 30 days of annual leave – for a balanced work-life experience.

About us The Independent Research Group Receptor Biochemistry, led by Dr. Mariana Schuster, is dedicated to understanding and engineering the molecular decisions that determine whether a plant gets sick, focusing on the proteases deployed by plants and pathogens and the proteins they cut. We are small, international and deliberately interdisciplinary. People here come from plant science, biochemistry, chemistry and computational backgrounds, and much of the useful thinking happens in the conversations between them. The IPB is a non-university research institute of the Leibniz Association on the Weinberg Campus of Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg, a foundation under public law under the direct supervision of the state of Saxony-Anhalt. Around 200 people work here, including about 40 doctoral researchers, across four scientific departments and two independent research groups. Research at the IPB aims to understand the (bio)chemical basis of plant resilience and performance in challenging environments related to climate change. The IPB offers excellent research facilities and state-of-the-art infrastructure, including in-house mass spectrometry. More at ipb-halle.de. Halle (Saale) is a green, walkable city with a large student population, low living costs by German standards, and fast connections to Leipzig and Berlin.

Dr. Mariana Schuster
Head of Research Group
Telefon:
Mariana.Schuster@ipb-halle.de

Leibniz-Institut für Pflanzenbiochemie (IPB)
Weinberg 3
06120 Halle (Saale)
